evidence.title: Abroad with Two Yanks
evidence.text: Abroad with Two Yanks is a 1944 American comedy film directed by Allan Dwan and starring Helen Walker, William Bendix and Dennis O'Keefe as the title characters.

evidence.title: Abroad with Two Yanks
evidence.text: It was Bendix's third and final role in a film as a US Marine and the first of Dwan's three films about the United States Marine Corps.

evidence.title: South Sea Rose

evidence.title: South Sea Rose

evidence.title: South Sea Rose

evidence.title: George Marshall (director)

evidence.title: David Harum (1915 film)
evidence.text: David Harum is a 1915 American silent comedy-drama romance film written and directed by Allan Dwan, produced by Famous Players Film Company and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

evidence.title: David Harum (1915 film)
evidence.text: It is based on the 1899 novel of the same name by Edward Noyes Westcott and the 1900 Broadway play based on the novel, starring William H. Crane (Crane also starred in two subsequent Broadway revivals).

evidence.title: David Harum (1915 film)
evidence.text: Crane agreed to star in the film (which was his debut) only if the film was written exactly as the play.

evidence.title: David Harum (1915 film)
evidence.text: "David Harum" is the only film of Dwan's for Famous Players that still survives.

evidence.title: David Harum (1915 film)
evidence.text: A print is preserved at the George Eastman House in Rochester, New York and the Cinémathèque Française in Paris.

evidence.title: 15 Maiden Lane
evidence.text: 15 Maiden Lane is a 1936 American crime film directed by Allan Dwan and starring Claire Trevor and Cesar Romero, with Lloyd Nolan.

evidence.title: 15 Maiden Lane
evidence.text: The plot involves an insurance investigator (Trevor) who infiltrates a gang who had stolen jewels from the eponymous building on Maiden Lane in the Fulton Street District of Manhattan.

evidence.title: 15 Maiden Lane
evidence.text: The neighborhood had been the center of New York City's Diamond District since the 19th century before its gradual relocation uptown to 47th Street after World War II.

evidence.title: 15 Maiden Lane
evidence.text: The Museum of Modern Art in New York City screened a restored print of the film in June 2013 as part of an Allan Dwan retrospective.

evidence.title: The Habit of Happiness
evidence.text: The Habit of Happiness is a 1916 American silent comedy film directed by Allan Dwan and filmed by cinematographer Victor Fleming.

evidence.title: The Habit of Happiness
evidence.text: The film was written by Allan Dwan and Shannon Fife from a suggestion by D. W. Griffith and stars Douglas Fairbanks.

evidence.title: The Habit of Happiness
evidence.text: A 16mm print of the film is preserved in a private collection.
